abstract: During the diauxic transition, Saccharomyces cerevisiae must preserve mitochondrial genome integrity while remodeling mitochondrial architecture for respiratory growth. The transcription factors Nrg1 and Rtg3 form a heteromeric regulator previously shown to be required for mitochondrial DNA maintenance, but its mitochondrial targets remained unknown. Here, we identify ILV5 and MGM101, which encode mitochondrial nucleoid proteins, as Nrg1-Rtg3 targets. Both factors occupied these promoters, with Rtg3 binding independently and recruiting Nrg1, providing a direct regulatory link to mitochondrial DNA maintenance. Unexpectedly, electron microscopy revealed that loss of either factor caused severe cristae defects even during fermentative growth, and these defects were more pronounced after the diauxic transition. Nrg1-Rtg3 also switched from repressing ATP20, ATP21, and MIC60 during fermentative growth to activating them after the transition. At the ATP20 promoter, recruitment dependence also reversed across the diauxic transition, from Nrg1-dependent recruitment of Rtg3 during fermentation to Rtg3-dependent recruitment of Nrg1 after the transition. Even as this dependence reversed, both factors remained necessary to establish the wild-type chromatin organization associated with each transcriptional state. Together, these findings show how one transcriptional complex can maintain activation of mitochondrial nucleoid genes while switching the regulation of cristae-organizing genes as cells transition to respiratory growth.
